text:
sophia (sales): FYI ACME just asked if we can bump their GPU quota for a customer demo tomorrow morning in eu-west-1. They need ~12 GPUs for ~3 hours. Current quota is 4.
ben (support): Thanks Sophia — are they doing long-running batches or low-latency chat? any peak RPS / tokens estimates?
ops-bot: :rotating_light: region eu-west-1 GPU pool currently at 92% capacity; queue depth +120 requests. Last 10m tail latency 520ms.
ram (eng-infra): @ben @sophia can you share expected concurrent reqs and model size? if it's many short chats, admission control + concurrency bump might be better than raw GPU quota.
sophia (sales): It's a demo with ~30 concurrent users generating ~200 tokens each, model = 13B. So ~6k tokens/s peak across the session. Demo window 09:00-12:00 CET. It's timeboxed.
ella (eng-sre): Queueing/backpressure is expected at that utilization. If we naively give 12 GPUs we risk starving other customers unless we reserve capacity. Two options: 1) temp reserved capacity (preferred) 2) increase per-org concurrency to let requests queue across existing pool. Both have cost tradeoffs.
ben (support): I can open a quota override but need cost center + approver. Also need exact duration and start timestamp.
elinor (finance): Please put cost center and estimated spend. Our temporary burst cost is billed at on-demand uplift rate.
sophia (sales): Cost center ACME-PROOF. Estimated uplift ~€1.2k for 3h on 12xA100 equiv. If you reduce to 8 GPUs it's ~€800.
ram (eng-infra): Quick cluster check: with current autoscale cooldown + node spinup time we won't be able to spin 8 new nodes in <12m in eu-west-1. We should pre-provision by calling the reserved pool API and pin to scheduling tag.
ella (eng-sre): Also recommend model variant quantized-int8 to reduce per-token compute. That will drop latency and queueing.
ben (support): To speed this up, run this command in infra-ops (we'll run it):
```bash
/quotas override --org "ACME" --region eu-west-1 --gpus 8 --duration 4h --reason "Customer demo - preapproved by ops-lead" --cost-center "ACME-PROOF"
```
ops-bot: Quota override request 0x9f2 created (pending approver). Link: https://redwood.internal/quotas/0x9f2
mike (ops-lead): I can sign off on 8 GPUs for 4h. Approving on the condition infra uses quantized model and routes demo traffic to the reserved tag. :thumbsup:
ben (support): Noted. I've added mike as approver. @ram can infra pre-provision nodes and apply scheduling tag "acme-demo-176999"?
ram (eng-infra): Starting pre-provision now. Will also set an admission-control rule to cap ACME concurrency to 50 so they don't monopolize the pool — they'll have fair share.
ell a (eng-sre): small correction: "ella (eng-sre)": I'll add a temporary bypass for health-checks and ensure KV cache warmup script runs against the quantized weights.
ops-bot: Pre-provision job started. Expected time to ready: ~14 minutes.
support-bot: Quota override 0x9f2 approved by mike (ops-lead). Override applied: +8 GPUs from 2026-04-21T08:45:00Z to 2026-04-21T12:45:00Z. Monitor: /dash/regions/eu-west-1
sophia (sales): Amazing, thank you team. I'll confirm schedule with ACME and tell them to use the demo link.
elinor (finance): Chargeback noted to ACME-PROOF. ETA for billing entry: next invoice run.
ram (eng-infra): Nodes are up and tagged acme-demo-176999. Admission control rule in place. I'll keep an eye on queue length and kv cache hit rate.
ella (eng-sre): Monitoring checklist: 1) tail latency 95p < 700ms 2) token cost per request  < baseline*1.3 3) fallback model reactive rule enabled.
ben (support): Closing loop — I've added the thread to the incident/ops playbook as a temporary-capacity event for post-mortem in case we see regressions.
sophia (sales): :raised_hands: thanks everyone!
ops-bot: Reminder: override 0x9f2 will auto-expire in 4h. Use `/quotas extend 0x9f2 --reason "extra time"` if needed.
